dayz-model-pipeline: a translation's offset counts lengths of its axis, not metres (#88)

references/animations.md section 5 rule 3 said "Axis vector doesn't define scale; only
direction matters" for every axis, and the examples read translation offsets as metres.
Read on 2026-10-03: Binarize keeps a translation's offsets as model.cfg writes them and its
axis at its own length (CocaLab: offset1 = 1 on 12-16 mm axes reads 1.0 in its binarized
tray). If the m249's older binarizer (ODOL v54) did the same, the vanilla m249's offsets
(-1..0 on 1.1 cm belt axes, 0..+1 on an 8.34 cm bolt axis, 0..+1.45 on a 10 cm magazine
axis) only make sense in axis lengths; its rotation axes are unit vectors. The rule now
separates rotation from translation (offset times axis length, inferred and not measured in
game; on a 1 m axis the offset reads in metres), the examples say they assume a 1 m axis,
troubleshooting gains the symptom, and a dated note qualifies "Multiple animations fight"
with the m249's bone bindings. Claim CLAIM-MODEL-TRANSLATION-AXIS-LENGTH; replaced sentences
quoted in dated notes. Docs only.

dayz-persistence, rigorous-data-audit: a registry entry leaves by its id, never by proximity (SP-456) (#97)

SP-456: dayz-persistence gains Hard stop 9 and a section for a mod's own
registry of world entities (sidecar JSON). From SecretRock's audit DZ-R9
(2026-10-03): an unregister that fell back to the nearest entry of the same
class within 0.75 m deleted a neighbour's entry whenever an entity without an
id was deleted; an unregister needs a matching id, an entity without one
never touches the file, an id two entries share identifies neither
(CLAIM-PERS-UNREGISTER-BY-ID: with that rule, in game on DayZDiag
1.29.163709, a console entity 0.3 m from a registered one was created and
deleted, the registry kept its SHA-256 and the registered one came back).
Restore binds by id: GetObjectsAtPosition3D promises no order, and a
position match proves nothing; a candidate without the entry's id is a
conflict to log, neither bound, given state nor duplicated ([DESIGN];
CLAIM-PERS-RESTORE-BIND-BY-ID). A restore pass still queued is removed
before the shutdown flag is set (CLAIM-PERS-SHUTDOWN-QUEUE). The
rigorous-data-audit entry-point audit gains the worked example, the
invariant's entry points and a search for proximity used as identity.

commit.message:
Refresh model providers and tune Sol 6.1 DM effort (#791)

* Update current OpenAI, ChatGPT, and Anthropic model support

Add GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Luna, GPT-6 Sol, Claude Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, and Sonnet 5.5 with current pricing, limits, and tier defaults. Preserve older model entries and saved tier assignments.

Upgrade the bundled Codex runtime to 0.160.0. Paginate account model discovery, route backend model IDs, retain advertised reasoning capabilities, and refresh saved ChatGPT catalogs through connection checks without requiring reauthentication.

Support current reasoning effort and Anthropic thinking modes, preserve OpenAI encrypted reasoning history, and account for cache-write usage. Update picker availability behavior, provider docs, and regression coverage.

Validation: 3993 tests passed (14 skipped), lint and typecheck passed, Windows SEA build and packaged boot probe passed. Authenticated read-only ChatGPT catalog and ephemeral tool-thread probes passed without inference calls.

* Set model-specific medium effort for the Sol 6.1 DM

Add optional per-agent effort defaults to known model entries and resolve them using the actual runtime model. GPT-6.1 Sol now uses medium for DM calls; other models and agent roles retain their existing defaults.

Preserve explicit loop and named-agent developer overrides, including null, and retain the historical default-key fallback for unnamed agents. Update setup resolution, documentation, and precedence regression coverage.

Validation: 4006 tests passed with 14 skipped; lint, typecheck, and diff checks passed. Live Sol 6.1 gameplay validation follows in the isolated campaign fixture.

* Require known identities in scribe handoffs

A DM could receive canonical identity feedback and later hand the same referent to the small-context scribe using a new descriptive phrase. Exact identity prefetch did not match that phrase, so the scribe could create duplicate people or items despite the DM already knowing their UIDs.

Require known UIDs beside recurring or re-described referents in the DM directive and scribe tool descriptions. Retain established names or aliases when no UID is known, without adding a lookup turn or exposing internal handles in narration. Tell the scribe to bind each associated description to its supplied UID, and synchronize the tool/subagent catalogs.

Validation: 92 focused tool-registry, scribe, and prompt-loading tests; npm run typecheck; npm run check (4006 passed, 14 skipped, lint passed); git diff --check. No campaign data or model calls changed.

* Preserve ChatGPT model identity and reasoning capabilities

A saved ChatGPT catalog-row ID could reach the provider loop before being translated to its backend model ID. The registry then treated it as unknown and dropped configured reasoning or the Sol 6.1 DM medium default. Resolve runtime identity inside the existing transport retry boundary before capability and effort selection, without rewriting the saved assignment. Forward resolution through recording wrappers and preserve catalog-row aliases across discovery, connection refresh/deduplication, provider construction, and REST serialization.

A failed model/list request previously cached empty capabilities for the entire subprocess. Clear only that failed cached promise so later requests retry, and guard against late failures clearing a newer cache after disposal. Distinguish an explicitly empty supported-effort list from absent metadata: the former omits effort and summary overrides; the latter retains legacy compatibility behavior.

Regressions cover old row pins through real tier and recording wrappers, default/explicit/null effort wire requests, dual legacy-connection merges, refreshed alias serialization, separate-request catalog retry, a late failed discovery after disposal, empty effort capability wire omission, and startup resolution backoff.

Validation: 165 focused tests; npm run check (4014 passed, 14 skipped, lint passed); npm run typecheck; git diff --check. All provider-wire tests use injected RPC fixtures; no paid model calls, game data, credentials, or saved user assignments changed.

fix(time): cap over-max HP at CE turn boundaries

CE lets transference (and polymorph) push HP above max at hit time, then
caps the player at the end of playerTurnEnded (Time.c:2857-2864) and
each monster when its turn comes due (Time.c:2717-2723). The port had
neither cap, so a ring of transference could keep the player above max
indefinitely. Both caps are added in CE order, including the early-fall
path; terrain death now returns before the fall check as in CE.

Two old fixtures set HP above max directly; they now also raise maxHp
(single-variable counterfactual recorded), assertions unchanged.
Known remaining gap (not changed here): CE ends the game immediately
with "Drained by a cursed ring" on lethal negative transference.

scribe, persist a complete frozen scene-prefix tree, and deliver terse

Update API/client views, campaign-explorer, diagnostic scripts, prompts, and
